source_scope: Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p.268, PDF p.278.
source_reading: The printed Edinburgh marriage register identifies Thomas Glasgow as a merchant when he married Catharine Weir on 12 October 1643. This is the same named couple as the already-held OPR index (685/1/430/252, FR856) and the parents in the Edinburgh baptisms of 1644–1650. The occupation is newly incorporated from the inspected printed page; the marriage date was already in the research findings. The previous complete proposed biography incorrectly retained an estimated 1644 marriage, so it is corrected to the indexed 1643 event.
limitations: The printed register is an edited transcription of parish records, not a newly inspected manuscript. It supplies no father, mother or witnesses. Merchant is a useful identity discriminator, but does not establish descent from John Glasgow-1030 and Jonet Mathie. The separate Thomas Glassford, merchant, marrying Catharine Thomsone on 14 July 1637 on the same printed page is a comparison only: different surname and wife; no remarriage or identity merge is established. The 1660 gratis burgess identification remains probable. Father confidence remains 22%; no relationship confidence increase is recorded.
next_test: Seek the original 12 October 1643 Edinburgh marriage entry, merchant guild/council property records, or a testament naming Thomas the merchant’s father or siblings. Do not repeat the completed Findmypast birth-window and printed apprenticeship searches without a new variant or source.
